# B 台风/飓风风场（主力方向，一级节点）

## 目标
Liang Hu 主力方向。Liang Hu 多年做三维边界层台风风场模型：参数模型用于抗风设计风速与快速计算，WRF 类降尺度用于单次台风预报/后报，延伸到集合预报与韧性/性能。本节点判断 AI 气象/气候大模型接到这条链上哪几处值得投入，按子方向分子节点推进。

## 子方向（Liang Hu 10-14 定）

# B Typhoon/hurricane wind fields (primary direction, tier-1 node)

## Objective
Liang Hu's primary research direction. Liang Hu has spent many years developing 3D boundary-layer typhoon wind field models: parametric models for wind-resistant design wind speeds and fast computation, and WRF-class downscaling for single-typhoon forecasting/hindcasting, extending to ensemble forecasting and resilience/performance assessment. This node evaluates where along this pipeline connecting AI weather/climate foundation models is worth investing in, advancing via sub-nodes organized by sub-direction.

## Sub-directions (Set by Liang Hu on 10-14)
| # | Direction | Status | Node |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B1+B4 | AI track/intensity (including ensembles) → parametric boundary-layer wind field (using literature models until Liang Hu's model is ready) → station peak winds vs. ASOS, benchmarked against NHC; plus AI ensembles to examine spread | Shelved (10-14); v2 preparation paused: after enforcing strict station type and anemometer height filters (8–12 m), only 13 events × ≥3 stations remain; recount after Liang Hu's model arrives or the 2026 season is ingested | |
| B2 | Design wind speeds and long-term risk: synthetic typhoons (including AI-generated synthetic typhoons) + 3D boundary-layer models | Shelved (10-14 22:30); attribution finalized on 10-15: severely underestimated nearshore Cat3+ passage rate is the root cause, which switching wind field models cannot rescue | |
| B3 | Single-typhoon WRF forecast/hindcast driven by AI large-scale fields (typhoons only; see K for thunderstorms) | Not started (~early-to-mid November) | 10-14 reply: can commit, queued after the first Wister pair and Node K; K will first establish the "AI fields → WPS intermediate format → WRF" pipeline for B3 to reuse; division of labor: the Lab provides AI/GFS fields, WRF bot runs WPS/real/WRF; recommends 9/3 km two-way nesting; a single run costs tens to over a hundred SU → run on CRC (exceeds the Lab's ≤50 SU per-job cap on TACC); select events from the B1+B4 event list. **Pre-launch gate (set by Root Lead on 10-15)**: (1) first ask whether reusable typhoon/hurricane WRF cases or configurations exist; (2) estimate SU (single-node CRC runs are also accounted in SU; multi-node runs go to TACC); if a single job exceeds 50 SU or reaches production scale (>24 h or ≥200 SU), it requires a promotion proposal or handoff to the WRF line, to be confirmed with Liang Hu by Root Lead. Given the estimate of tens to over a hundred SU per run, it will **very likely exceed 50 SU → expected to go through a promotion proposal / handoff to the WRF line**. All supercomputer jobs require a resource request + registration, pre-check and submission separated into two commands, and `ssh -n`. **Must be included at kickoff handoff**: the HRD dropsonde 10–300 m typhoon profile dataset (backed up on CRC) can serve as a WRF boundary-layer profile verification set (over-ocean / inner-core, not overland) |
| B5 | Resilience and performance (Liang Hu: do not lower priority; feasible and publishable, though of slightly lower intrinsic scientific value—unverifiable and low reliability) | Not started | Start after B1/B4 wind field ensembles and Node I (loss database) yield results |

## Current Status
10-14 evening: B1+B4 v1 failed the 48 h gate and was shelved (6/6 support)—cannot conclude whether AI tracks are better or worse: both pipelines underestimated 48 h winds by 35–38%, primarily due to pre-registered size/pressure input assumptions (Δp0 scaling, frozen RMW), while track effects had inconsistent signs. Verified by Node B Lead. Because the core question remained unanswered, B1+B4 was dispatched to run a v2 feasibility check (R1 operationally available size inputs, R2 ≥15 events; output files only without gate evaluation) before deciding whether to launch v2. B2 Grok quick search returned (used as leads only, unverified): existing design wind speed studies all rely on hybrid methods, as free-running AI weather/climate models produce overly weak typhoons; accordingly, Node B2 was launched: pass RAFT (40,000 synthetic typhoons with ML intensity, CC BY 4.0, Zenodo verified by Node B Lead) and STORM through the same H08 wind field model to compare 50-/700-year return period wind speeds at coastal stations against ASCE 7-22. B3 is scheduled for ~early-to-mid November. No rush on Liang Hu's model; use literature models first.

## Finalized Decisions
- 2026-10-14 Accepted shelving of B2 (failed Gate 1 with RAFT at 30.95%); dispatched a pre-restart diagnostic comparing inputs against observations only, without generating new ASCE comparisons → 
- 2026-10-14 Accepted shelving of B1+B4 v1; dispatched v2 feasibility check; dispatched Grok quick search for B2 first → 
- 2026-10-14 Combined B1 and B4 into a single sub-node (sharing the same events, wind field model, observations, and scripts; split B4 out later if ensemble size grows) →

**原因**
RAFT 目录在美国沿岸几乎不出 3 级以上（Cat3+）的强飓风，墨西哥湾最严重。

站点 100 km 内的 Cat3+ 过境次数，按每千条风暴算：

| 海岸段 | RAFT | STORM | 观测（HURDAT2） |

| 得州 | 0.09 | 1.04 | 3.45 |
| 路易斯安那到佛州狭长地带 | 0.17 | 1.45 | 4.14 |
| 佛州半岛 | 1.97 | 2.55 | 2.07 |
| 卡罗来纳 | 0.42 | 2.66 | 3.45 |

- **偏低的分段对得上**：哪几段过境率偏低，700 年风速就在哪几段偏低。
- **和 STORM 比**：RAFT 近站的风暴次数其实多 27%，但其中强飓风只占 6% 左右，STORM 是 16%，问题出在强度尾部。和实测比，RAFT 的次数和强飓风占比都偏低。

这一步只和实测路径（HURDAT2）比，没碰 ASCE，也没用超算。下表是站点 100 km 内、过境时达到 3 级以上的风暴数，按每 1,000 条风暴计：
